DriverModule now uses inclusive intervals including zero-size and readable empty-name modules; pointer values use the native layer mask. FullDllName is never queried for ownership.

Unreadable BaseDllName skips that module as in SSDT; native reporting still includes a partial diagnostic. Traversal is now forward-only with full LIST_ENTRY readability and containing-object validity checks. Module scalar failures, missing-page diagnostics and resource limits are not a fully aligned fault contract.
Unreadable MmSystemRangeStart now uses the reference architecture default without an extra partial diagnostic; absent symbols still fail.

Driver names use direct NameInfo.Name.String / ServiceKeyName.String / DriverName.String. Missing-name values agree on tested inputs, but native still reports individual read faults as partial where reference catches them silently.
Only x86 and x64 are supported. Further kernel builds, malicious hidden-driver samples and damaged-input coverage remain outstanding.

generator_vectors.scope: Actual DriverModule generator, SSDT builder/ModuleCollection and DriverScan get_names_for_driver. Synthetic module scalars/names and already-scanned driver objects isolate interval ownership, pointer domain, empty/read-fault names, independent fallback and known exceptions. generator_vectors.links_scope: Actual LIST_ENTRY.to_list with synthetic pointer and layer validity adapters; tests forward-only traversal, ignored Blink, non-head cycles, null and unreadable pointers, containing-object validity and unaligned links. Native counterparts run real fixture page tables and captured reads.
generator_vectors.native_coverage: All 50 cases exercise real fixture memory/pool scans in both physical and virtual modes. Equality is tested separately at the generator admission and stricter upstream scan gate. Additional native cases cover maximum-zero, odd UTF16, masked and readable user-half extension pointers and alias multiplicity.
